note.text: Producers fix energy into organic material, usually through photosynthesis. Consumers obtain food by eating organisms or their products. Food-chain arrows point from the food source towards the consumer, showing transfer. Decomposers break down dead organic matter and help return nutrients to available pools. Energy flows through the system and much becomes dispersed heat; nutrients can cycle between organisms and the environment. A fixed transfer percentage is a teaching assumption, not a law applying to every link.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to trace energy flow and nutrient cycling and calculate a transfer using an explicitly assumed efficiency. Builds on: ecosystem components and interactions. Leads to: biomes and responses to environmental change.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: A model chain in a grass plot is grass → grasshopper → frog. The arrow from grass to grasshopper indicates feeding and transfer towards the consumer. Dead material from every level can enter decomposition, not only material from the last consumer. Removing vegetation can affect food, shade, habitat and soil, so consequences can spread through more than one pathway.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Follow each arrow and state what moves. Distinguish energy transfer from mineral nutrient recycling: decomposers do not send all lost heat back to plants as usable food energy. For a percentage model, calculate the fraction of the stated input and retain kJ as the unit. Predict a possible effect, then identify evidence needed to test it.

questions.prompt: A simplified food-chain model has {input} kJ available at one trophic level and assumes {rate}% transfers to the next. Calculate the transferred energy. The percentage is a model assumption, not a universal rule.

misconceptions.explain: That treats the percentage as a whole-number multiplier and omits division by one hundred.
That repeats the percentage rather than calculating an energy amount.
That assumes complete transfer, contrary to the stated percentage.

solution: Multiply the available energy by the assumed fraction.
